Class 3 · Chapter 7 of 10

Shopping totals and better buys

Add prices, find change, compare pack prices and choose within a budget.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Time, timetables and dates. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can total prices and find change.
  • I can compare pack prices.
  • I can choose within a budget.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Add the prices

A basket has items at Rs 50, Rs 20 and Rs 5.

Add them: 50 + 20 + 5 = Rs 75.

Screen 2 of 4

Find the change

You pay Rs 100 for goods that cost Rs 64.

Change = 100 − 64 = 36. You get Rs 36 back.

Screen 3 of 4

The better buy

Pack A is 4 pencils for Rs 20. That is Rs 5 each.

Pack B is 6 pencils for Rs 24. That is Rs 4 each. Pack B is the better buy.

Screen 4 of 4

Stay in budget

You have Rs 60. The things you want cost Rs 45.

Rs 60 − Rs 45 = Rs 15 left. You are inside the budget.

Words to know
total
All the prices added together.
budget
The most money you plan to spend.
better buy
The choice where each item costs less.

For parents

What your child learns

Change is the money paid minus the price. To find the cost of many items, multiply the price by the number. To compare packs, find the price for one item in each pack.

A common slip

Children may compare total prices of different sized packs. Find the cost of one item for each pack. The smaller one-item cost is the better buy.

5-minute home activity: Better buy

  1. Write 2 stickers cost Rs 14 and 3 stickers cost Rs 24.
  2. Divide to find the cost of one sticker for each.
  3. Say which pack is cheaper per sticker.
  4. Work out the price of 8 caps at Rs 31 each.
